content.text:
Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

Fix GitHub issue #265 in Moneo. In the desktop smoke test (`npm run desktop:smoke`, scripts/desktop/package-smoke.mjs), the check `quit stops every process` failed on mac-arm64 in the Desktop workflow for PR #253 (actions run 43915218876, job 133467406741, log `smoke-mac-arm64` artifact). It reported a leftover `Moneo#65851`. Windows and Linux passed. The server port was closed after quit.

1. Read the logs: `gh api repos/indkhan/Moneo/actions/jobs/133467406741/logs`, and download the `smoke-mac-arm64` artifact with `gh run download 43915218876 -n smoke-mac-arm64`.
2. Work out which process outlived quit. Moneo#<pid> is likely an Electron helper or a child the app spawned. Then work out why:
   - Look at the main process's quit/shutdown path in desktop/src (backend processes in desktop/src/backend/processes.ts and index.ts), and at how the smoke test samples processes.
3. Fix the shutdown cause: every child is stopped and awaited before the app exits. If the cause is really in the check, for example sampling a process while macOS is still reaping it, fix the check so it waits for exit deterministically rather than by sleeping, and explain why.
   - Don't simply retry the check or loosen it.
4. You can't run macOS here. Reason from the code and logs. Make the fix platform-neutral where possible, and add a unit test in desktop if the shutdown ordering is testable (see desktop/src/backend/processes.test.ts).
5. The Desktop workflow runs on PRs that touch `desktop/` or `scripts/desktop/`. Make sure it runs on your PR, and check the mac-arm64 smoke result with `gh pr checks`. GitHub's Apple Silicon runners are scarce, so if the job is cancelled for lack of a runner, rerun it with `gh run rerun <id> --failed` once the run finishes.

## Rules
- Read AGENTS.md (the Desktop app section) and desktop/README.md first, and follow them.
- Branch `t3/issue-265-mac-quit` from current `origin/main`. Commit each step, ending each message with:
  Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Don't end your turn while a command or CI run is still going.** Wait in the same turn.
- **Never kill a process you didn't start yourself in this session, verified by PID.**
- Run one `npm ci` at a time. If it stalls, retry once with `--prefer-offline`.
- Never test against the owner's installed app or its user-data folder. Set `MONEO_DESKTOP_HOME` to a scratch folder.
- **Run `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` yourself and quote their last lines in your final reply.** Also run `npm test`.
- Push and open a PR to `main` (`Closes #265`), ending the body with:
  🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
  Never merge.
- Final line: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.

git add scripts/desktop && git commit -q -m "Desktop smoke: wait for Moneo's processes to exit after quit instead of sampling the instant the main process ends

On macOS the Chromium helpers of the main process are reaped by the system a moment after the main process exits, so sampling immediately saw a live helper (Moneo#65851 in run 43915218876). Quit now waits, bounded, until every sampled process is gone; a real leak still fails the check after the wait.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git push -q -u origin t3/issue-265-mac-quit 2>&1 | tail -2
gh pr create -R indkhan/Moneo --base main --title "Desktop smoke: wait for processes to exit after quit (mac-arm64)" --body "Closes #265

mac-arm64 reported \`quit stops every process — Moneo#65851\` in run 43915218876 while the server port was closed and Windows and Linux passed.

**Cause.** The log shows the app's own children stopped and awaited in order (\`Next server stopped\`, \`Backend stopped\`, \`Stopped\`) before \`app.exit(0)\`. The leftover is named \`Moneo\`: the smoke labels processes by the first word of the command, so it is a \`Moneo Helper (…)\` Chromium process (renderer, GPU or utility) the app does not spawn itself. On macOS those helpers are orphaned when the main process exits and reaped asynchronously, and the check sampled liveness the moment the main process ended. Windows and Linux tie helpers to the parent, so they were already gone. I couldn't run macOS here, so this is reasoned from the log and code.

**Fix.** \`Desktop.leftRunning()\` waits (polling, bounded at 30 s) until every sampled process has exited, then returns whatever is still alive. Used by the quit checks in \`package-smoke.mjs\` and \`package-journey.mjs\`. A real leaked process (backend, Next server) still fails after the wait. No sleep, no retry of the check.

No unit test: the change is in the packaged-app harness, and the shutdown order in the app itself is unchanged.
